  "rule": "K-S2",
  "applies": "yes",
  "applies_why": "The judge labels the Isaiah 7:14 dispute UNDERDETERMINED because the challenger addressed the virgin and young-woman wording while the defender addressed the prophetic application, turning on one verse having two aspects or senses.",
  "verdict": "BREACH",
  "quote": "D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- Challenger answered the virgin and young-woman wording in [DR3] and defender answered the prophetic application in [CR2] and [CR3].",
  "rule_words": "That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand. This is about one verse. It does not apply when the judge weighs two chains.",
  "room": "Phrase: This is about one verse. It does not apply when the judge weighs two chains. Reading A: the judge treated Isaiah 7:14's wording and application as two aspects of one verse, so K-S2 applies and forbids UNDERDETERMINED. Reading B: the judge weighed two separate chains, challenger wording versus defender application, so the exception would make K-S2 inapplicable.",
  "why": "The judge made UNDERDETERMINED rest on the single verse Isaiah 7:14 having a wording side and an application side, which K-S2 forbids because a verse with two senses is not open and both senses stand."
